title: Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility — Payer Class Register
content:
Every coverage record Summit Ridge Home Medical holds for a patient belongs to one of seven payer classes of **Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility**. The register below fixes, for each class, three standing attributes: the payer family it belongs to, the priorities in which it may sit on a patient account, and how its benefit year is reckoned.

## Register

| Payer class | Payer family | Priorities the class may take | Benefit year reckoned by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | Medicare fee-for-service | primary only | calendar year |
| Medicare Advantage HMO | Medicare Advantage | primary only | calendar year |
| Medicare Advantage PPO | Medicare Advantage | primary only | calendar year |
| Medicaid Fee-for-Service | Medicaid | primary or secondary | calendar year |
| Commercial HMO | commercial | primary or secondary | plan year |
| Commercial PPO | commercial | primary or secondary | plan year |
| Medicare Supplement Plan G | Medicare Supplement | secondary only | calendar year |

## What each column means

- **Payer family.** The payer family the class belongs to decides which notice, appeal and cost-share regime applies to the class.
- **Priorities the class may take.** These are the priorities in which the payer class may sit on a patient account: a primary-only class is only ever primary, a secondary-only class is only ever secondary, and a class marked primary or secondary may hold either position.
- **Benefit year reckoned by.** This is how the benefit year for the deductible and out-of-pocket accumulators is reckoned: by the calendar year, or by the plan year.

## Reading the register

- A Commercial PPO record and a Medicaid Fee-for-Service record can each be found in either position on an account; an Original Medicare Part B record is never found in the secondary position, and a Medicare Supplement Plan G record is never found in the primary position.
- The two commercial classes are the only classes of Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility whose accumulators follow a plan year; the other five follow the calendar year.
